# WO-2026-08-15-03 — restore the render gate, and the eight gates dying behind it

**What is actually wrong, established by a read-only diagnosis you should trust but verify:**

`render-vm-check.mjs:1919` pins a mutation anchor to an exact opening tag,
`'<div class="page page-pad">'`. On 2026-08-13 (`51b9a3b`, *"WP-B15-49: Mum's SEND becomes real"*)
that tag legitimately gained a state binding and now ships as
`'<div class="page page-pad" :data-send-state="sendState">'` (`public/shopping.js:1004`).
The anchor guard exists for a good reason — without it the seven mutations would silently no-op and the
self-test would report seven vacuous "caught" rows — so it correctly refuses.

**The template is CORRECT. The tool's expectation went stale. Do not edit `shopping.js` to satisfy a test.**

**Why this is not cosmetic.** The CI step is:

```
node services/cockpit/render-vm-check.mjs --self-test
node services/cockpit/render-vm-check.mjs
```

under `bash -e`, so **line 1 exiting 1 means line 2 never runs — and line 2 is the only invocation that
inspects the real templates.** The failed step then fails the job, so **eight further steps have been
skipped on every push since 2026-08-13**: service-worker cache derivation, `down-reason-check`,
`provenance-check`, CAPAE, clone-portability, origin-boundary, `rotation-report-check`.

**Mum's shopping surface has had no other CI coverage** — `shopping-geometry-check.mjs` and
`names-check.mjs` appear in no workflow at all. So her screen has been ungated for two days, and her SEND
shipped in that window.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — The anchor matches what ships, and survives the NEXT attribute.** Repair
`render-vm-check.mjs:1919` to anchor on a **stable stem** rather than a full opening tag — the same
lesson this file already learned and recorded for `DRAWER_STEM` at lines 360-369. A literal swap to
today's tag would go red again the next time anyone adds an attribute to that div.

**AC2 — The mutations still actually mutate.** After the repair, prove each of the seven household
mutations changes the template — **assert the mutated text DIFFERS from the source**, so a future
no-op is caught by the test rather than by a reader. A mutation that silently fails to mutate is the
exact defect the anchor guard exists to prevent, and the repair must not weaken that guard.

**AC3 — `--self-test` passes end to end**, with its executed count reported. Do not reduce the
mutation set to make it pass.

**AC4 — THE REAL GATE RUNS, and you report what it says.** Execute
`node services/cockpit/render-vm-check.mjs` (no `--self-test`) against current templates and **report the
result honestly**. **If it FAILS, that is a finding, not a failure of this order** — it would mean a real
defect has been sitting unguarded on Mum's screen since 2026-08-13. **Do not fix that here.** Report it
with its exact output and stop. Repairing whatever it finds is a separate decision.

**AC5 — The other two ticking anchors are reported, not necessarily fixed.** The same brittleness exists at
line 1765 (`'<div class="app-view">'`) and at line 1872 (the rotation Elapsed-row anchor). If converting
them to stable stems is genuinely trivial and provable, do it. If not, **report them** — do not leave them
unmentioned, and do not turn them into a project.

**AC6 — CI proves it, not your laptop.** Push and show the `cockpit-private-apps` job on your branch
reaching the second invocation and running the steps that have been skipped since 2026-08-13.
**An absent run is indistinguishable from a green one — this whole finding is that principle biting.**

## Required evidence

**Exit codes captured UNPIPED, real output pasted beside every claim.**

- `node services/cockpit/render-vm-check.mjs --self-test` — before your change (exit 1, showing the anchor
  failure) and after (exit 0, with its executed count).
- `node services/cockpit/render-vm-check.mjs` — the real gate, with its full verdict.
